title: Adaptive decode-windowing with speculative kernel pegging
creator: Connor Li
description:
Goal: Reduce p95/p99 tail latency for mixed short/long request workloads by improving how prefill and decode queues select kernels and shape admission windows. We will implement an adaptive decode-windowing algorithm that speculatively pegs incoming requests to a small set of candidate kernel/attention lanes based on a short warm-up probe, then finalize kernel assignment late in the prefill phase when sequence-length and KV cache pressure are clearer. This reduces mis-pinned kernel handovers during decode and enables tighter batch shapes without inducing stragglers.

Background: Current continuous-batcher often commits kernel paths early which leads to inefficient kernel switches when actual decode length differs from estimate. Kernel switches (especially between fused-attention and quantized paths) cause head-of-line stalls and inflate p99. Additionally, short-lived bursts of short responses are batched with long decodes causing padding-induced slowdowns.

Approach:
- Lightweight probe: run a micro-prefill (up to 8 tokens) in a low-overhead mode to collect attention-mode hints (sparse vs dense usage, kv-cache delta). Probe must cost <1ms on average and be cancellable.
- Speculative pegging: maintain a ranked candidate list of kernels per request slot (e.g., [fused-amp, quant4x, fallback-torch]) with confidence scores from probe + historical profile. Initially allocate into lanes by candidate rank to encourage homogeneous batches.
- Late-binding commit: at prefill completion threshold (first 32 tokens or when estimate crosses a threshold), commit kernel assignment; perform light-weight slot reshuffle within the same GPU to coalesce similarly assigned requests, avoiding full migration cost.
- Adaptive decode-windowing: instead of fixed admission windows, compute a per-tenant decode window size derived from recent length distribution and current GPU utilization. Smaller windows for tenants with short-mean lengths to avoid polluting long batches.
- Graceful fallback: if commit-time reshuffle is too costly or exceeds a latency budget, fall back to existing kernel with a metric logged for investigation.

Success metrics: p95 reduce by >=10% and p99 reduce by >=15% on mixed workload benchmark; tail SLO breaches reduced by 50% for production-like traces. Maintain within 3% throughput loss and <2% increase in average token cost.

Out-of-scope: full cross-GPU request migration, kernel rewriting.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end integration test demonstrating late-binding commit without head-of-line deadlocks
Benchmark run on mixed short/long trace shows >=10% p95 and >=15% p99 improvement versus baseline
No more than 3% throughput regression on sustained steady-state long-only workloads
Instrumentation emits per-request probe latency, candidate confidence, reshuffle cost metrics
Feature gated behind runtime flag and tenant opt-in for initial rollout
design_notes: Probe design must avoid materializing KV cache for probe tokens; use synthetic cache-delta estimator
Candidate ranking model is simple logistic regression trained on historical prefill profiles; initial model persisted as small table in runtime config
Reshuffle uses intra-GPU slot swap using lock-free handoff to avoid memory copies
Attention-optimization hints include sparsity estimate, head-utilization skew, and per-layer memory footprints
implementation_plan: Week 1: implement probe path and low-overhead metrics (Connor)
Week 3: late-binding commit + intra-GPU reshuffle; add feature flag (team)
Week 4: run synthetic benchmarks and iterate on thresholds; enable tenant opt-in for performance team
Week 5: rollout canary to 10% of tenants and monitor SLOs; collect regression signals
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: probe overhead increases latency —> mitigate by strict microbudget and sampling 10% of requests initially
Risk: reshuffle causes transient spikes —> add reshuffle cost guardrail and abort reshuffle if estimated CPU or copy time exceeds budget
Risk: model misclassifies leading to persistent tail skew —> fallback to conservative pegging and increase probe frequency for that tenant
benchmarks: Baseline trace: mixed_shortlong_v3 (10k requests) — baseline p95=72ms p99=210ms
Proto run (speculative pegging enabled, small reshuffle): p95=62ms (-14%) p99=172ms (-18%); throughput -1.7%
Canary run notes: observed 0.9% token-cost increase for quant4x fallback cases; acceptable per SLO
